appearance.organs.leaf.shape.sinus.why: A cordate blade's two rounded basal lobes reach back past where the petiole meets it, either side of the petiole, leaving a notch between them; a reniform blade's, broader, reach farther; a blade of any other shape has none.

appearance.organs.basal.shape.sinus.why: A rosette's leaves are the species' leaves, unless their own are stated: a cordate blade's two rounded basal lobes reach back past where the petiole meets it, a reniform blade's farther; any other has none.

appearance.organs.leaf.shape.fan.why: A palmately veined blade's main veins leave the top of its petiole together, the midrib and two more a side fanning out across it (into its basal lobes where it has them); a pinnately veined blade's leave the midrib along its length.

appearance.organs.basal.shape.fan.why: A rosette's leaves are the species' leaves, unless their own are stated: a palmately veined blade's main veins fan from the top of its petiole, two a side with the midrib.

appearance.organs.leaf.hairs.colour.why: A blade's hairs are drawn in the colour they are stated in; white where none is.

appearance.organs.basal.hairs.colour.why: A rosette's leaves are the species' leaves, unless their own are stated: a blade's hairs are drawn in the colour they are stated in; white where none is.

appearance.organs.leaf.hairs_beneath.col.why: A blade's underside's hairs are drawn in the colour the plant's hairs are stated in; white where none is.

appearance.organs.basal.hairs_beneath.co.why: A rosette's leaves are the species' leaves, unless their own are stated: a blade's underside's hairs are drawn in the colour the plant's hairs are stated in; white where none is.

appearance.stem_hairs.colour.why: The hairs on young stems and leaf stalks are drawn in the colour the plant's hairs are stated in; white where none is.

appearance.organs.leaf.shape.apex_taper.why: A blade narrows to its tip as its apex is stated, over its last three tenths: with hollow sides drawn out (acuminate, caudate), straight sides to a point (acute), fuller and blunt (obtuse), rounded, or cut square (truncate); a mucro, cusp or bristle stands on a rounded or blunt tip, and a notched tip is rounded.

appearance.organs.leaf.shape.apex_point.why: A caudate blade ends in a tail, a cuspidate one in a short sharp point, a mucronate one in a tiny point and an aristate one in a bristle, beyond the blade's tip.

appearance.organs.leaf.shape.apex_notch.why: An emarginate blade's tip is notched along its midrib, a retuse one's shallowly.

appearance.organs.leaf.shape.base_taper.why: A blade widens from its base as its base is stated, over its first three tenths: a long hollow taper (attenuate), a straight wedge (cuneate, acute), fuller (obtuse), rounded, or cut square (truncate).

appearance.organs.basal.shape.apex_taper.why: A rosette's leaves are the species' leaves, unless their own are stated: a blade narrows to its tip as its apex is stated, over its last three tenths: with hollow sides drawn out (acuminate, caudate), straight sides to a point (acute), fuller and blunt (obtuse), rounded, or cut square (truncate); a mucro, cusp or bristle stands on a rounded or blunt tip, and a notched tip is rounded.

appearance.organs.basal.shape.apex_point.why: A rosette's leaves are the species' leaves, unless their own are stated: a caudate blade ends in a tail, a cuspidate one in a short sharp point, a mucronate one in a tiny point and an aristate one in a bristle, beyond the blade's tip.

appearance.organs.basal.shape.apex_notch.why: A rosette's leaves are the species' leaves, unless their own are stated: an emarginate blade's tip is notched along its midrib, a retuse one's shallowly.

appearance.organs.basal.shape.base_taper.why: A rosette's leaves are the species' leaves, unless their own are stated: a blade widens from its base as its base is stated, over its first three tenths: a long hollow taper (attenuate), a straight wedge (cuneate, acute), fuller (obtuse), rounded, or cut square (truncate).

appearance.foliage.why: The plant's leaves are drawn in the colour a grown leaf's upper side is stated in.

appearance.foliage_shade.why: In deep shade the stated leaf colour darkens as every look's own colour does.

appearance.bark.why: A grown stem's bark is drawn in the colour it is stated in.

generator.params.leaves_per_node.why: A node bears one leaf where the leaves alternate, a pair where they are opposite, and the taxon's count where they are whorled.

generator.params.divergence.why: Each node turns from the one below by the golden angle in a spiral, half a turn in two ranks, a third of a turn in three, and half the gap between its own leaves where pairs or whorls cross. Where the turn and the leaves are stated at different ranks and disagree, the leaves decide: pairs and whorls cross even under an order's spiral, and single leaves under an order's crossing pairs turn by the golden angle.

generator.params.flower_branches.why: A herb's flowering stem bears a flowering side branch in the axil of each of its top leaves, as many as the taxon states.

generator.params.stem_height.why: A herb's stems grow back each year to about the plant's usual height.

generator.params.height_max.why: A conifer's leader, or a columnar succulent's stem, rises with age toward the tallest the plant grows and never passes it.

generator.params.crown_height.why: A broadleaf tree's or shrub's crown fills out with age toward a top as high as the tallest the plant grows.

rules.appearance.organs.leaf.shape.sinus.note: The chart of plane shapes names cordate and reniform blades by their bases: two rounded lobes either side of a notch where the petiole joins, a reniform blade broader than long. How far the lobes reach back (0.15 and 0.2 of the blade's length) is the model's choice.

rules.appearance.organs.basal.shape.sinu.note: The chart of plane shapes names cordate and reniform blades by their bases: two rounded lobes either side of a notch where the petiole joins, a reniform blade broader than long. How far the lobes reach back (0.15 and 0.2 of the blade's length) is the model's choice.

rules.appearance.organs.leaf.shape.fan.note: Ingrouille (Diversity and Evolution of Land Plants, p. 15 of the PDF): in palmate venation several main veins fan out from the blade's base, where in pinnate venation the laterals leave a midrib along its length. Two a side beside the midrib (five main veins) is the model's choice of a common count.

rules.appearance.organs.leaf.shape.apex_.note: Simpson (Plant Systematics, pp. 526-527 of the PDF) classes apices by the angle where the apical margins meet: acuminate and caudate with hollow sides under 45 degrees, acute 45 to 90, obtuse over 90, truncate about 180, rounded curved. Drawn as the power of the narrowing over the blade's last 0.3 (the model's choice): 1 straight, 2.2 hollow, 0.6 blunt, 0.35 rounded, 0.12 square.

Ingrouille (Diversity and Evolution of Land Plants, Fig. 1.2, p. 16 of the PDF) draws a mucronate tip with a tiny point, a cuspidate one with a short sharp point and an aristate one with a bristle; Simpson adds the caudate tail. Their lengths (0.025, 0.04, 0.08 and 0.15 of the blade) are the model's choice.

Simpson (Plant Systematics, p. 526 of the PDF): a retuse apex is notched to 1/16 of the way to the midrib, an emarginate one 1/16 to 1/8; drawn about 0.012 and 0.03 of the blade's length deep, the blade's half-width being about a quarter of its length.

rules.appearance.organs.leaf.shape.base_.note: Simpson (Plant Systematics, pp. 524-526 of the PDF) classes bases by the angle where the basal margins meet: attenuate under 45 degrees, cuneate 45 to 90, obtuse over 90, truncate about 180, rounded curved. Drawn as the power of the widening over the blade's first 0.3 (the model's choice), as at the apex.

rules.appearance.foliage.note: How PlantGen colours an organ from the colour a source states for the species, a choice of the model's (visual forms Skill 3, 2026-10-14): the stated colour itself, on the looks' 0 to 1 scale.

rules.appearance.foliage_shade.note: How PlantGen shades foliage in the colour a source states for the species' leaves, a choice of the model's (visual forms Skill 3, 2026-10-14): the stated colour darkened by the generator's own shade factors (0.35, 0.42 and 0.55 of red, green and blue, as a look with a colour of its own is shaded, src/looks.rs).

rules.appearance.bark.note: How PlantGen colours an organ from the colour a source states for the species, a choice of the model's (visual forms Skill 3, 2026-10-14): the stated colour itself, on the looks' 0 to 1 scale.

traits.note: Vascular plants are built of stems and leaves with vascular tissue, and most hold to their ground by roots: ferns form large leaves and branching roots, and by the late Devonian plants had vascular tissue, well-defined leaves and root systems (Biology 2e, 25.4). The few without roots or leaves, such as the whisk ferns, which lack both, say so in their own files.

rules.note: What the words mean, as accounts of phyllotaxis such as Okabe and colleagues' use them: a spiral or two-ranked shoot bears one leaf at a node, a decussate one a pair and a whorled one three or more. A spiral turns about the golden angle (137.5 degrees) from node to node and two ranks half a turn; pairs and whorls alternate, each standing over the gaps of the one below, half the gap between its own leaves round (90 degrees for pairs). Three ranks turn a third of a turn, as their name says.

rules.generator.params.flower_branches.note: What the herb program's flowering side branches mean: a branched herb such as fennel or poison hemlock (Abrams 1951 pp. 231, 241: branched, much branched) carries an inflorescence at the end of each side branch from its upper leaf axils, as many as the taxon states; a herb that states none keeps one inflorescence to a stem.

rules.generator.params.stem_height.note: What the herb program's stem height means: each year's stems reach it at maturity, give or take height_spread, their flowers included, so a mature herb stands about as tall as a flora's usual height for the plant, read as the range's middle unless it names a typical height.

rules.generator.params.height_max.note: What the conifer and succulent programs' height_max means: the height their Chapman-Richards curve rises toward with age and never reaches, so the tallest the plant grows, the height a flora gives as its greatest ("trees to 40 m"). Plants of a usual age stand below it, as the curve says. Where a flora's greatest is a rare record, the plant grows a little tall; a check of the grown plant against its usual height (spec rework M8) will show it.

rules.generator.params.crown_height.note: What the broadleaf program's crown_height means: the top of the space the crown may fill, which rises with age at crown_rate toward it and never passes it, so the tallest the plant grows, the height a flora gives as its greatest. Where that greatest is a rare record, the plant grows a little tall; a check of the grown plant against its usual height (spec rework M8) will show it.
